title: Round 19 / frontier I: last literature long shots (Mahalanobis-Mallick Problem L, isogeny distance to structured curves)
question: (1) Does the Mahalanobis-Mallick linear-algebra formulation of ECDLP ('Problem L', and their 2026 zero-minor follow-up) admit any solver below sqrt(p), or does it reduce to known exponential costs? (2) For a generic prime-order curve, what is the cost of walking an isogeny path to a curve with exploitable structure (j=0/1728, small embedding degree, anomalous), and is any such target reachable in less than sqrt(p)?
rationale: Remaining untested routes named by the round-17 literature survey (priors ~1%).
success_criteria: Exact statements; reproducible evidence; honest negatives.
resource_limit: One bounded subagent; no recursion; no commits.
